prompt:
Implement `AutomationClient.java`, a single-file Java client for the VCF Automation 9.1 project-change scenario described by `docs/contract.json`. The local contract is derived from Broadcom's official xAPI reference pages; it is reference documentation, not a published API specification. Use only the Java standard library and always use the base URI and bearer token supplied to the constructor.

`TestMain.java` expects a public final `AutomationClient` with `AutomationClient(URI baseUri, String bearerToken)` and these public nested records: `ProjectSummary(String id, String name)`, `ProjectUpdate(String name, String description)`, `Tag(String key, String value)`, `ZoneAssignment(String zoneId, int priority, int maxNumberInstances)`, `StepResult(String operation, int statusCode, boolean succeeded, String message)`, and `ChangeReport(List<ProjectSummary> projects, List<StepResult> steps, boolean complete)`. Implement `ChangeReport applyProjectChange(String projectId, ProjectUpdate project, List<Tag> resourceTags, List<ZoneAssignment> zoneAssignments) throws IOException, InterruptedException`.

Each call must first fetch the project collection, then PATCH the named project, PATCH its resource metadata, and PUT its zone assignments, using the methods, paths, authentication, media type, and JSON shapes in the contract. Return project summaries sorted lexicographically by name and then id; the service does not promise collection order. Execute the three changes in order. Do not erase successful steps when another change fails: return one `StepResult` per change with the contract operation id, actual HTTP status, success flag, and an empty message for success or the service's `message` for failure. `complete` is true only when all three changes succeed. Encode the project id as one URI path segment and JSON-escape caller-provided strings. Do not contact or special-case any VMware host.

Run `python3 verify.py` to exercise the client against the contract-pinned loopback service. The verifier includes a deliberately failing zone update; service failures represented in the returned report are not verifier failures.
